utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon to everyone. We are now in session. Mr. Registrar, could you kindly call the case of the current hearing.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Good afternoon, everybody in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-98-32/1-A, the Prosecutor versus Milan Lukic and Sredoje Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Milan Lukic, can you hear and follow the proceedings in a language that you understand? THE APPELLANT M. LUKIC: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Sredoje Lukic, can you understand the proceedings in a language that you understand? THE APPELLANT S. LUKIC: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I would now like to turn to the parties and ask them to introduce themselves. And I would like to start with the Office of the Prosecutor, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Kyle Wood and Virginie Monchy for the Prosecution, along with our case manager, Colin Nawrot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I would now like to turn to the Defence counsels for Mr. Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. I am Tomislav Visnjic, with Mr. Dragan Ivetic, and together with Vladimir Bozovic, our legal consultant, and Dalida Chrysostomidou. We are representing Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I would now like to turn to the Defence counsel of Mr. Sredoje Lukic, and I would like them to introduce themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. I'm Djuro Cepic, Defence counsel for Mr. Sredoje Lukic. Today, appearing with me on my left-hand side, my learned friend Mr. Jens Dieckmann as co-counsel, on my right-hand side, Ms. Sabine Schulz, our legal assistant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. The Status Conference was convened pursuant to Rule 65 bis (B) and (C) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of the Tribunal, which requires that a Status Conference shall be convened within 120 days following the filing of the notice of appeal, and thereafter within 120 days after the last Status Conference. The main purpose of a Status Conference is to give any person in custody pending appeal to raise issues -- the possibility to raise issues in relation thereto, including the physical and mental condition of that person. The first Status Conference hearing was held on the 13th of November, 2009. We then met for a second Status Conference on the 16th of March, 2010, and for a third time on the 14th of July, 2010. We are, therefore, meeting today for the fourth Status Conference as part of the appeals procedure in the present case. I would like to recall the parties that the Appeals Chamber is still seized of three confidential motions written by the Defence of Mr. Milan Lukic. They are dated, respectively, 8th of February, 2010, 10th of February, 2010, and 22nd of February, 2010, in which it is considered to grant Milan Lukic the possibility to introduce additional evidence in appeal. I would also like to inform the parties, as I did during our last meeting, that the Appeals Chamber will issue a single decision on all three motions before the appeals hearing. Lastly, the date set for the appeals hearing, which was supposed to be on the 21st of September, 2010, had to be postponed. It is difficult at the moment to set a specific date for that hearing, but I do think that this hearing should not be convened before the month of February 2011. The Appeals Chamber will officially set the appeals hearing date in due time, and will determine the time granted to each party in order for them to make their submissions. I would now like to turn to Mr. Milan Lukic and to Mr. Sredoje Lukic to ask them to inform me about their detention conditions and state of health. I would now first like to turn to Mr. Milan Lukic. Mr. Lukic, do you wish to inform me about any particular concern with regard to your detention or with regard to your health? THE APPELLANT M. LUKIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, please allow me to thank you, first of all, for giving me the opportunity to point to some of the most recent developments which are making my life, which is already difficult, even harder in the Detention Unit. Before I tell you what the problem is, I would like to inform you that I'm going to do everything to stay dignified and proud until the end, because that is something that my stainless reputation and peaceful conscience allows me to do. I'm no killer. I'm given particular strength by the faith that the Appeals Chamber, respecting the rules of the profession and law, will be able to lift all the injustices that I have been subjected to by the Trial Chamber. You are my only hope and my last chance in my attempt to have the truth established on the basis of facts and to satisfy justice, justice primarily towards those who were subjected to misfortunes in the past wars and justice in relation to me, who found himself without willing in the whirlwind of war. Those who contributed the most to charges against me, I hope, will be found out in order to protect themselves in relation to all of their crimes. I am primarily thinking of Brane Savic and Risto Perisic, officials who are still pursuing their charges against me. Any time when there are any particular chances of some criminal proceedings being charged -- being issued against them, this happens. Over the past few weeks, the discovery of bodily remains in the Perucac Lake has been topical over the last few days. Nothing is known about these remains, their origin, how they managed to get there, but the media, directed by Savovic and Perisic, immediately began to harangue, at my expense and regarding my involvement, even though some officials from Bosnia-Herzegovina had said that some of the bodily remains that were found originate from the First and the Second World War. This media campaign relentlessly keeps naming me as the commander of the paramilitary formation such as white Eagles and so on, even though in this trial it has been proved that my role came down to the duties of the plainest reserve policeman who was mobilised as part of his compulsory war assignment, which applied to all conscripts, including myself. Even the Trial Chamber, on the weight of the evidence, had to conclude in the judgement that I was no commander, no leader of any paramilitary formations. Your Honour, in view of the need for me to be as rational as possible in my time allotment, I just mentioned a few things on this occasion. Having this in mind, I most kindly ask you to grant me and to make it possible for me, through the media, to address the public of Montenegro, Serbia, and Bosnia and Herzegovina, and the whole international community, about facts, about many questions, and, in particular, questions on which I had never been able to express my position. I'm disturbed by the fact that certain events from that time, of which I was acquitted at domestic courts of any responsibility, still the media in Bosnia-Herzegovina, in Montenegro, continually ascribe these acts to me. Those media have placed themselves above the Court, above the law. Simply, this would be the only way for the other side to be heard in this case, to have my arguments stated publicly. I feel that this is my duty towards those victims and their families, who were casualties of the war, as well as a duty towards those people who know the truth but still are not allowed to talk. Giving me a chance to speak with journalists from Montenegro, Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, you would, in the best way, contribute to justice and the truth and would give me a little more strength to fight to continue to prove my innocence before this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Lukic --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Milan Lukic, would you be kind enough to talk about your detention conditions or your physical and mental state of health. UNIDENTIFIED SPEAKER: There's no translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you hear me now? No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can Mr. Sredoje Lukic hear me? THE APPELLANT S. LUKIC: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Everything is fine. I don't know whether you can hear me, whether the interpretation is on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe you could use the microphone. Can you hear me now? Fine. THE APPELLANT M. LUKIC: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I shall repeat what I've already stated. Mr. Milan Lukic -- Mr. Milan Lukic, would you be kind enough to talk to us about your detention conditions and your physical and mental state of health, and could you please try to be as brief as possible. Thank you. THE APPELLANT M. LUKIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the media is lynching me, so I can't feel well in the Detention Unit. They keep circulating lies about me in the media. Therefore, I do not feel well, and I wanted to point this out to you, asking you to allow me to defend myself. Otherwise, what else could I do? Your Honour, as you could see, my request is modest and minor, and I hope you will have the understanding for this request. Thank you, once again, for allowing me to address you and for having the patience to listen out to me. Once we have the appeals hearing, I will have a lot to say publicly. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thank you, and I take note of your concerns. I take note of the concerns you've just informed us about, and I would like to thank you for your co-operation. Mr. Sredoje Lukic, would you like to raise any issue about the detention conditions or your state of health? THE APPELLANT S. LUKIC: [Interpretation] As I have just said to you, Your Honour, I would like to thank you. Everything is fine. There are no problems whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And, lastly, I would like to ask the parties if they have, at this juncture, any issues which they would like to raise as we sit in this Status Conference. I would like first to turn towards the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: The Prosecution has nothing at this time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I now turn to the Defence counsel of Mr. Milan Lukic. Would you like to raise a particular issue?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No new issues, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. And I would like now to turn to the representative of the Defence -- the counsel of Defence of Mr. Sredoje Lukic. Would you like to raise any issue at this juncture?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, for this opportunity. No new issues will be raised from our side. Just for the record, if you leave me -- we received translation in B/C/S, in our language, and I have to say we are aware that the authoritative version is in English, but the version in B/C/S has got translation problems regarding to the main issues for my client. Of course, we solved that issue, but, as I said, just to put it in the record of the Status Conference. And also just to add that we join to the proposal of Prosecutor which the Prosecutor raised on the Status Conference during the March 2010 with request for the information of oral hearing, six weeks prior to commencement of oral hearing. Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Of course, what you've just stated will be part of the record. Thank you. I have no other questions to raise, and I believe that we can adjourn for today. I would like to thank the parties for their participation, and I would also like to thank the staff of the Tribunal for helping us in organising this Status Conference. The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: at 3.21 p.m.
